Use case: identity-preserve. Production 2D fighting game animation sprites. Image1 canonical DAICHI master; image2 his design poster. Preserve exact adult male face, tied hair bun and cloth headband, sturdy broad body, lamellar torso and shoulder armor, forearm protection, worn light kimono and armored skirt over hakama, shin wraps, sandals. His single weapon is a LONG STRAIGHT YARI SPEAR: wooden shaft with straight double-edged metal spearhead and small bell/tassel near butt. NOT a katana, naginata, axe or staff without point. Both hands on spaced shaft grips. Grounded disciplined defender, calm firm weight, functional armor, not berserk or acrobatic.
Create EXACTLY EIGHT full-body poses in TWO COLUMNS by FOUR ROWS on a PORTRAIT canvas. Read sequence row by row. Every character faces RIGHT in consistent side/three-quarter fighting camera. Same body scale, costume, weapon length and anatomical identity in all cells. Each figure AND ENTIRE spear, butt to point, inside its own large cell with generous empty gutters. No cell touches another. Genuine transparent background. Pure monochrome ink artwork matching master, opaque white highlights; no text, labels, grid, shadow, ground, color, dust, motion blur or effect lines.
Sheet1 GUARD AND WALK. Row1 cels1,2: canonical stable guard, spear diagonally down-right held in both hands as master, subtly breathing with planted feet. Remaining six cels3-8: six sequential phases of a complete measured forward walking cycle, knees softly flex, short weighted steps, rear foot gathers and passes, front foot settles, then returns to initial gait. Torso stays solid and spear stays controlled. Actual distinct leg and fabric poses. Armor plates move subtly with body. Preserve spear's complete length even if figures need to be smaller in each cell.
